title: Connected depth-two puncture with nonempty principal slice
statement: Let R be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth], g an element of its maximal ideal, and W the complement of the closed point in Spec R [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then W is connected and its inverse image in Spec(R/(g)) is nonempty.

proof.text: Apply depth-two Hartogs restriction to the structure module on Spec R. It is quasi-coherent and finite on affine opens. Its module stalk is linearly equivalent to the local ring, and the closed stalk ring is isomorphic to R. Transport regular sequences across these equivalences to verify the boundary-depth hypothesis. The unit at the top open makes restriction Gamma(Spec R,O) to Gamma(W,O) bijective.

Depth is bounded by Krull dimension, so dim R is at least two. Choose a strict chain of three primes from Order.le_krullDim_iff. Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.exist_mem_one_of_mem_maximal_ideal, a consequence of the principal ideal theorem, gives a nonmaximal prime containing g. Quotient prime correspondence yields a point of Spec(R/(g)) over W. Thus the principal slice, and consequently W, are nonempty.

The global-sections comparison identifies Gamma(W,O) with the local ring R. Local rings have only the idempotents zero and one. The scheme connectedness criterion in terms of global idempotents therefore makes W connected.

lean.statement:
theorem depth_two_punctured_principal_slice_connected
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (g : R) (hg : g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := R) R)
    (W : (Spec (.of R)).Opens)
    (hW : ∀ x : Spec (.of R), x ∈ W ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) :
    let j := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g})))
    ConnectedSpace W.toScheme ∧ Nonempty (j ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme
